context:
Goal: every device gets the tracking update.
Problem (rule): after you restore a backup, the restored tracking value has no new time stamp, so the server's newer tracking can overwrite it at the next sync; a decision says a later reply cannot undo a restore, so only you can allow this exception.
Based on (ruling): decision a-restore-is-not-local: a later server reply cannot undo a restore.
Based on (read): src/merge-rules.mjs, where the restore re-stamps check-ins, stamps and envelopes only, not tracking.
Based on (read): the coordinator's plan with the refuter's check: each line carries an optional tracking time and the later time wins; the saved-state rule allows an optional defaulted field inside a key already saved.
Departs from: main lets a restore stick on the restoring device — option a lets newer server tracking win after a restore.
Waiting on: your answer; the coordinator builds with a as the working default meanwhile.

options.gain: No phone rebuild; tracking is shipping data from the source.
options.how: Tracking gets a time only when it is imported; a restore keeps the old time.
options.label: Leave the restore alone
options.lose: A restored tracking value can be overwritten once by the server's newer one.

options.how: The restore gives every tracking value the restore's time.
options.label: Stamp tracking on restore
options.lose: The phone's rules bundle changes, so the phone app needs a rebuild and an install.

short: Restore and tracking: let newer win or stamp it
title: After a restore, may the server's newer tracking overwrite the restored tracking?
why: Tracking comes from the source file, so a one-time overwrite costs little and saves a phone rebuild (coordinator's recommendation).
